result.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
result.summary: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. However, a single agentic task often combines easy and difficult subtasks, making one model choice for the entire task inefficient. We introduce partial routing, which guides a frontier lead model to delegate suitable subtasks to a cheaper worker model. From both models' past runs, we identify recurring subtasks and measure each model's quality and cost on them. These measurements produce delegation guidance, with a parameter, $δ$, controlling how much is delegated. The lead decides when and what to delegate during execution, without training either model. On held-out tasks from ViBench and Terminal-Bench 4.0, partial routing achieves higher mean task performance than the lead alone and task-level routing. With $δ= 0.75$, it raises the lead's ViBench score from 70.2 to 78.5 at 19% lower cost, and its Terminal-Bench pass rate from 54% to 61% at similar cost. Giving the lead only the subtask breakdown, without a worker, also reduces cost on both benchmarks and raises the Terminal-Bench pass rate. These results show that analysis of past runs can support more efficient planning and more effective delegation, with little cost and implementation overhead.

AI.brief_summary: 研究 agentic workflow 中的「部分路由」：让前沿主模型按历史运行中识别的重复子任务，把合适子任务委派给更便宜的 worker 模型，并据质量与成本生成委派指导，无需训练模型。在 ViBench 和 Terminal-Bench 上，该方法优于单一主模型和任务级路由，并降低部分成本。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按子任务质量与成本决定「何时外包计算」的机制，可能为 LVR 中动态计算分配、THINK/LOOK/STOP 的成本收益权衡提供方法线索；但路由信号能否对应视觉推理步骤仍需核查。
